subject: Life Skills
title: Emotional Hijacking
description: A micro-lesson that makes Emotional Hijacking usable.

hook.text: He sent a furious reply-all email at 11 PM. By morning, he wished he could unsend it.

buildup.text: Daniel Goleman coined 'amygdala hijack.' When threat is perceived, the emotional brain overrides the rational one.

discovery.text: The hijack lasts about 20 minutes. After that, your prefrontal cortex regains control and perspective returns.

twist.text: The trigger is rarely the real issue. The email that enraged you tapped an older wound — a past humiliation or fear.

climax.text: Create a 20-minute rule: when emotions spike, delay any response. Walk, breathe, or draft without sending.

punchline.text: Feel everything. Send nothing for 20 minutes.

quiz.question: How long does an amygdala hijack typically last?
